name: Reverse Collar (short stock + long call + short put)
summary: The mirror image of a collar built on a short stock position: a long call caps the unlimited upside risk and a short put below finances it, capping the downside gain.

legs.strike_rule: call delta 0.20-0.30, above the short entry (the ceiling)
|put delta| 0.20-0.30, below the short entry (the funding leg and the floor)

max_profit: (short entry - put strike + net credit) x 100
max_loss: (call strike - short entry + net debit) x 100 - defined on the upside by the long call
breakevens: short entry + net debit per share (or minus the net credit)

greeks.gamma: positive near the long call strike, negative near the short put
greeks.theta: near zero when built for zero cost

when_to_use: INCLUDED FOR COMPLETENESS - NOT TRADEABLE AT LEVEL 3 IN THIS SYSTEM. The combined three-leg overlay on a short position; the bank has the protective call and the covered put separately but never both on the same short.
entry_rules: BLOCKED: requires a short stock position plus a short put, which most brokers including Alpaca treat as needing level 4 short-option approval. Assume level 4 and reject at the router.
If ever enabled: confirmed borrow, borrow rate < 3% annualized, no ex-dividend date inside the option's life (the short seller owes the dividend).
Call strike <= short entry x 1.10 so the defined upside loss is <= 10% of notional.
Put strike >= the bearish price target; the structure gives up everything below it.
Net cost <= 0.3% of share notional; both option legs same expiry, OI >= 250.
management_rules: Roll both option legs together at 21-30 DTE.
Roll the whole structure down after a decline of more than 2 x ATR(14) to re-center the band.
If the short put's delta exceeds 0.60, close it and accept the unfinanced long call - the trade has already made its money.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: the short put is the only assignable leg; flatten it by 15:30 ET on expiration day whenever it is ITM. Assignment buys 100 shares, which closes the short position at the strike - the intended max-profit outcome, but at the counterparty's timing, not yours.
Close the short put at extrinsic < $0.10 or |delta| >= 0.85.
Close the long call rather than exercising it; exercise would buy shares and flatten the short at the ceiling.
Unwind all three legs as one combo whenever the share leg is covered.
assignment_risk: One assignable leg (the short put). Unlike the long-side collar, assignment here is convergent - it closes the short stock - but it is still an unplanned, un-timed position change, and the borrow and dividend obligations on the short shares run the whole time.
buying_power: Reg-T short stock margin (150% of proceeds) plus the put requirement, less the long call's protection. Level 4.
liquidity_needs: Borrowable name with a two-sided liquid chain at both strikes.
common_mistakes: Assuming it is the symmetric twin of a collar - the borrow cost, the dividend obligation and the hard-to-borrow buy-in risk have no analogue on the long side.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
